candidates.title: Application of generative and parametric design in the development of supporting software for industrial equipment
candidates.abstract: The development of auxiliary software for industrial equipment is often constrained by repeated customization, lengthy adaptation procedures, and difficulties in maintaining compatibility among heterogeneous devices. This paper presents a three-layer collaborative framework that combines parametric configuration with generative optimization techniques. The proposed framework consists of a Parametric Configuration Layer, a Generative Optimization Layer, and an Engineering Adaptation Layer, enabling reusable software components and more efficient equipment adaptation. In the proposed framework, Pro/E three-level family tables are employed for parameter mapping, while LLM-based PLC code generation, VADS-based visual inspection, and GA-based parameter optimization are integrated to improve the adaptability and operational efficiency of industrial systems. Standardized data exchange based on JSON format and MQTT communication is adopted to support information interaction between different layers. A Python-based graphical user interface (GUI) is also developed to integrate the functions of the three layers, allowing engineers to operate the system without directly managing the underlying software logic. The framework was evaluated using two industrial scenarios involving an intelligent machine tool and an automated sorting line. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces equipment adaptation time from 48 h to 6.4 h and decreases the overall software development cycle by 81.2%. Meanwhile, the visual inspection accuracy reaches 91.5%, and energy consumption is reduced by 15.3% compared with the conventional approach. The proposed framework allows different industrial devices to be integrated through reusable software modules, reducing the need for repeated development during equipment expansion. This provides a practical approach for deploying flexible software solutions in manufacturing environments.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering-Grade Parametric CAD: A Critical Review of Representations, Large Language Models, and Agentic Design Systems
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly expanding computer-aided design (CAD) from shape generation toward generative, conversational, and agentic engineering. However, most AI–CAD evaluations remain dominated by geometric similarity and execution success, while industrial CAD depends on editable parameters, design intent, stable feature histories, manufacturing constraints, and downstream CAD/CAE reuse. This structured critical review synthesizes 107 sources, principally from 2020–2026, across constrained sketches, boundary representations (B-Reps), parametric sequences, executable CAD programs, large language and multimodal models, CAD agents, commercial-CAD integration, and CAD–CAE. Rather than organizing the field only by model family, the review compares methods through the engineering information preserved and the behavior of generated models after modification. The synthesis identifies a consistent evidence gap: geometric validity and program execution are increasingly strong, whereas native feature-tree robustness, persistent references, design-intent preservation, and downstream verification remain weakly benchmarked. To address this gap, we propose the engineering-grade AI–CAD (EG–CAD) framework, in which geometric validity and executability are mandatory gates followed by parametric editability, constraint/design-intent preservation, feature-history robustness, engineering compliance, and downstream usability. A reference agent architecture and staged roadmap connect these criteria to CAD/CAM/CAE and smart-manufacturing workflows, reframing AI–CAD as an engineering automation problem rather than a shape-generation task.

candidates.title: Exploring an Agent-Based Generative AI CAD Framework Enhancing CAD Design Automation with AI-Driven Parametric Modelling and Adaptive Query Generation
DeciCAD: Harness-Grounded Learning of Action Policies for CAD Agents
candidates.abstract: Large Language Model agents operate through closed-loop action policies whose decision space is defined by an agent harness. We investigate how this operating space shapes agent behavior and policy learning in computer-aided design (CAD), a professional domain characterized by persistent state, geometric constraints, and long-horizon procedures. We instantiate this perspective in DeciCAD, a domain-native harness that exposes semantic CAD actions, decision-oriented observations, environment feedback, and persistent state transitions. Building on this harness, we develop a learning pipeline that extracts causal decision supervision from interaction trajectories and improves the policy through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and geometry-grounded online reinforcement learning (RL). Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD achieves the best F1 and intersection over union (IoU) while reducing model-output tokens by 45--88% relative to a general-purpose coding harness. Under matched supervision, its SFT policy improves F1 from 0.6883 to 0.7437 and outperforms the coding policy; subsequent online RL further raises geometry availability from 66.5% to 73.5% and F1 to 0.7880. These results demonstrate that the decision space induced by a harness materially affects both agent execution and policy learning in CAD.

candidates.title: Mechanical Design & CAD Explained: Engineering Design & Digital Modeling
candidates.abstract: Mechanical Design & CAD Explained: Engineering Design & Digital Modeling is an open-access, accreditation-aligned curriculum module developed under the PREP4UNI.ONLINE OER Initiative for undergraduate engineering candidates, mechanical designers, and STEM educators. Structured in accordance with the Washington Accord, EUR-ACE, and IEA Global Engineering Competency frameworks, this module bridges fundamental mechanics of materials with modern 3D CAD modeling, finite element simulation, and design for manufacturing. Key Analytical & Technical Coverage: Continuum Failure Theories: Von Mises distortion energy multi-axial yield criteria, Modified Goodman and ASME elliptic dynamic fatigue limits, and preloaded bolted joint compliance. Machine Element Synthesis: Circular power transmission shafting under combined torsion and bending, Marin endurance limit factors, stress concentration factors, and 1D worst-case vs. RSS statistical tolerance stack-up analysis. Digital Design Paradigms: Parametric feature modeling, generative topology optimization, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for real-time stress feedback, and Model-Based Definition (MBD) standards (ASME Y14.5 / STEP AP242). Applied Pedagogy: 4-column systems engineering trade-off matrix, seven cross-sector industrial failure case studies across aerospace, automotive, energy, and robotics, an interactive HTML5 canvas beam stress simulator, and six multi-step quantitative worked examples with explicit engineering interpretations. Curricular Attribution: Dr. Jacob Gan, PhD (Mich). PREP4UNI.ONLINE OER Initiative. Released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23339161.

candidates.title: INTEGRATION OF GENERATIVE DESIGN AND PARAMETRIC MODELING IN CAD FOR OPTIMIZATION OF AEROSPACE COMPONENT STRUCTURES
candidates.abstract: This paper discusses modern approaches to the design of load-bearing structures for aerospace equipment using topology optimization and generative design methods. The need to integrate parametric modeling to ensure the manufacturability of complex geometric shapes is sub-stantiated. It is shown that the application of additive technologies in combination with generative design allows reducing the weight of components by 40–50% while maintaining their strength characteristics.

candidates.title: Beyond overall accuracy: subgroup performance and threshold calibration of AI-assisted chest radiography for equity-oriented pulmonary tuberculosis screening
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence-assisted computer-aided detection (CAD) can expand access to chest radiography interpretation for pulmonary tuberculosis screening and triage, but high overall discrimination does not ensure safety at a deployed threshold. This focused narrative Mini Review synthesizes evidence on subgroup performance, threshold calibration, external validity, and implementation of CAD for adult pulmonary tuberculosis. Smear-negative, asymptomatic, and some HIV-associated disease may be less radiographically visible, increasing false-negative risk. Conversely, previous tuberculosis and competing chronic abnormalities reduce specificity and concentrate unnecessary confirmatory testing. Sex, age, geography, clinical setting, verification design, and software version can further alter operating performance. A numerical threshold is therefore not a portable algorithm property but a context-specific clinical resource-allocation policy. We propose a lifecycle in which programs define the intended use, lock the product and version, conduct representative local validation, select an operating point under explicit sensitivity and capacity constraints, audit clinically relevant subgroups, and monitor the complete care pathway. Stratified thresholds and multivariable models may improve selected settings, but current evidence does not justify replacing robust local calibration and governance. Prospective evaluations should compare threshold strategies under common verification standards and report missed cases, referral burden, treatment initiation, and patient-important outcomes.

candidates.title: Making What AI Cannot: Generative AI and Knowledge Through Making
candidates.abstract: Contemporary industrial designers have increasing access to Generative AI, computer-aided design (CAD), and fused deposition modelling (FDM) 3D printing. These tools can expand the possibilities available to individual designers, but their value cannot be understood only through the outputs they produce. This thesis examines how transferable knowledge can emerge through a practice-based design process that uses these tools, with particular emphasis on Generative AI. The research uses the design and fabrication of a free-standing loudspeaker as a vehicle for inquiry. Grounded in Research through Design and structured through Programmatic Design Research, the project was organised as a sequence of connected engagements involving visual and technical exploration, AI-assisted inquiry, CAD development, material experiments, comparative testing, practitioner feedback, fabrication, assembly, and reflection. Each engagement produced artefacts, observations, and takeaways that informed the direction of those that followed. The project demonstrates that transferable design knowledge was generated through the multiple interactions among these activities and shows how designer judgement emerged as a crucial part of the process, shaping how outputs were interpreted, which assumptions required proving, and which findings were rejected, revised, or carried forward. Generative AI supported exploration, technical questioning, comparison, and reflection, but its outputs were uneven and required further investigation through CAD, physical making, testing, and external feedback. CAD allowed possibilities to become controlled geometry while exposing material and assembly requirements. FDM printing brought these decisions into reality, revealing constraints involving tolerances, print behaviour, and material behaviour. The thesis argues that Programmatic Design Research provides a useful structure for turning these situated experiences into communicable and documented knowledge. By showing how ideas were generated, tested, rejected, revised, and carried between engagements, the research makes the design process open to reflection and extension by others. Its contribution is both the loudspeaker artefact and a transferable account of how contemporary tools, particularly Generative AI, can be investigated through contemporary industrial design practice.

candidates.title: TempFit: Panoptic Symbol Spotting via Template Fitting
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we introduce TempFit, a novel approach for the problem of Panoptic Symbol Spotting on CAD drawings. Existing methods treat symbol spotting as a per-primitive classification or mask-prediction task, with no explicit constraint enforcing that the primitives assigned to one instance form a spatially connected group. As a result, predictions may erroneously merge primitives from distant symbols into a single instance or fragment a coherent symbol across multiple predictions. Motivated by the professional "retrieve-and-transform" CAD design workflow, we reformulate this task as a Template Fitting problem, where each foreground instance is detected by retrieving and aligning a canonical template from a library, enforcing structural completeness by construction. Building on this formulation, we present an autoregressive transformer that unifies template retrieval and pose prediction within a single end-to-end pipeline. The framework treats the template library as an explicit geometric memory, parsing background regions in parallel via learnable background tokens and synthesizing foreground instances autoregressively while attending to template-specific geometry at each step. Experiments on FloorplanCAD and our newly collected IndustryCAD dataset, a more challenging benchmark with complex industrial symbols, heavy occlusion, and wide scale variation, demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with particularly large gains on IndustryCAD. Project page: https://tempfit-project.github.io/.

candidates.title: USE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DESIGNING ROBOTIC MODELS USING ENGINEERING GRAPHICS
candidates.abstract: The article examines the possibilities of using generative artificial intelligence in teaching the discipline “Engineering and Computer Graphics” in the design of robotic models for the processing industry. The feasibility of integrating generative artificial intelligence models into the design process of robotic systems as a means of developing spatial thinking, graphic competence, design skills, and digital skills of agricultural university students is substantiated. It is established that modern generative systems (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, Claude, DALL·E, etc.) support all stages of educational design, from developing technical specifications and generating product concepts to creating drawings and three-dimensional models, visualizing designs, preparing technical documentation, and analyzing possible design solutions. A methodology for using generative artificial intelligence in the educational project “Design of a Robotic Manipulator” is proposed. The methodology is based on the principles of project-based learning, STEM education, the competency-based approach, and the use of CAD systems. A structural model for integrating generative artificial intelligence into the process of graphic training has been developed. It includes the stages of problem formulation, concept generation, sketch creation, three-dimensional modeling, preparation of design documentation, and expert evaluation of the finished product. It is demonstrated that the use of generative AI contributes to increasing students’ motivation, developing engineering thinking, fostering digital literacy, and reducing the time required for routine operations in the design of robotic models.

candidates.title: Towards automatic digital garment assembly
candidates.abstract: Creating digital garments from existing two-dimensional patterns remains a time-consuming process. Although patterns are widely available in digital form, their assembly in garment CAD software involves manual definition of sewing operations and arrangement of the pattern panels for drape simulation. We present two learning-based approaches that automate both tasks using the 2D vector pattern as their sole input. Our automatic sewing model operates at the segment level, leveraging a Transformer encoder with multiple prediction heads. Our novel architecture supports many-to-many, ordered segment correspondences, as well as hems, overlapping seams needed for multilayer garments, and construction properties such as seam allowances and stitch types, required for the finished virtual garment but neglected by previous methods. A complementary panel-level model predicts body-region assignments, layers, and placement coordinates to initialize the drape simulation. We evaluate both models on a curated dataset of 4,035 professionally assembled garment instances. The sewing model exactly recovers all seam and hem topologies of 63.3\% of test garments, while the arrangement model meets the specified placement criteria for all panels in 66.2\% of test garments. We also integrate both methods into garment CAD software, demonstrating automatic assembly of successfully predicted garments.

candidates.title: Coarse-Graining Recursive Expert Computation: Continuation-Relative Interfaces and Failure Modes
candidates.abstract: Computational coarse-graining aims to replace a sequence of updates with a cheaper module while preserving task performance. We present a continuation-relative evaluation framework that assesses replacements through the computation that follows them, using downstream task quality and total execution cost as joint criteria. The framework distinguishes boundary representations, summaries of skipped computation, executed operations, and downstream loss. It makes interfaces and permitted deployment information explicit, combines fine-path references with directly trained controls using the same shortened architecture, and accounts for selection overhead. An exact loss decomposition separates replacement effects at a fixed downstream action from effects of changing that action. A finite construction shows how retained information can reduce the stipulated cost of zero-error prediction under fixed information and controller restrictions. Experiments in two frozen pretrained language models show that representation fidelity and task loss can favor different fitting objectives. In a prespecified comparison on a 1.7-billion-parameter model, next-token-loss training lowers in-distribution negative log-likelihood by 0.1901 nats per scored token compared with reconstructing the skipped blocks' output, using the same optimizer and update count. This ranking reverses in all nine paired comparisons under distribution shift. In a recursive expert prototype, the jointly adapted candidate lowers task error relative to frozen-bank and router-only baselines, but trails directly trained controls, and the tested input-only selectors fail the joint quality-cost criteria. Together, the protocol and studies provide explicit criteria and diagnostics for distinguishing useful computational replacement from local approximation gains within specified interfaces and evaluation settings.

candidates.title: Large language model-assisted CAD-RADS classification: structured report extraction, accuracy, and clinical decision-making risk of ChatGPT-4o/5 and DeepSeek-R1
candidates.abstract: Objective To compare ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 in assigning main Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categories from findings-only coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) reports and to characterize management-relevant classification errors. Methods This retrospective diagnostic-accuracy study included 2,100 category-balanced findings-only CCTA reports (300 per CAD-RADS category). Two experienced CCTA radiologists graded the English-translated reports; 12 disagreements were resolved by a third. ChatGPT-4o was evaluated in standard mode, ChatGPT-5 in Thinking mode, and DeepSeek-R1 in Deep Thinking mode; model generation and inference mode therefore varied together. Exact-match accuracy with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CIs), paired comparisons, and unweighted Gwet AC1 with 95% CIs were calculated. Management-relevant transitions and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) findings among high-risk downgrades were analyzed. Results DeepSeek-R1 had an exact-match accuracy of 82.57% (95% CI, 80.89–84.13) and AC1 of 0.797 (95% CI, 0.778–0.816). ChatGPT-5 had an accuracy of 80.19% (95% CI, 78.43–81.84) and AC1 of 0.769 (95% CI, 0.749–0.789), whereas ChatGPT-4o had an accuracy of 53.62% (95% CI, 51.48–55.74) and AC1 of 0.460 (95% CI, 0.435–0.485). Cochran's Q test was significant (Q = 657.87; df = 2; P < 0.001); after Holm correction, DeepSeek-R1 also outperformed ChatGPT-5 in the paired comparison ( P = 0.026), and both outperformed ChatGPT-4o (both P < 0.001). ChatGPT-4o downgraded 127/900 (14.11%) reference high-risk reports to CAD-RADS 3 or lower. Of these 127 cases, 65 underwent DSA within three months; DSA supported the original high-risk assessment in 56/65 (86.15%). The corresponding high-risk downgrade proportions were 37/900 (4.11%) for ChatGPT-5 and 23/900 (2.56%) for DeepSeek-R1. Conclusion The DeepSeek-R1 Deep Thinking and ChatGPT-5 Thinking configurations achieved higher accuracy than ChatGPT-4o in standard mode. Because model generation and inference mode varied together, the results do not isolate a model-family effect. LLMs merit further evaluation for secondary structuring when no documented CAD-RADS category is available, but should not overwrite a radiologist-assigned category or independently determine management.

candidates.title: CAD/CAM Technologies, Three-Dimensional Printing, and Contemporary Dental Materials
candidates.abstract: CAD/CAM technologies have transformed the production of fixed prosthodontic restorations from a craft based on manual skill into a standardized and measurable digital process. This chapter addresses, for dental students in their clinical years and for early-career clinicians, the fundamental principles of CAD/CAM systems, digital and artificial intelligence-assisted restoration design, milling and three-dimensional printing technologies, contemporary restorative materials, the factors influencing material selection, accuracy and quality control in digital manufacturing, and the biocompatible and smart materials of the future, in the light of the current and verified literature. The digital workflow comprises three interdependent links—data acquisition, design, and manufacturing—and the quality of the final restoration is limited by the weakest link in the chain. Although milling remains the gold standard for definitive restorations, additive manufacturing has become established for interim restorations, models, and surgical guides, and it is a rapidly maturing alternative for definitive restorations. On the material side, the rise of monolithic zirconia, the diversification of lithium silicate glass-ceramics, and the establishment of resin-matrix ceramics in minimally invasive applications offer the clinician a broad range of options with varying levels of evidence. Current systematic-review and meta-analytic evidence shows that AI-assisted design shortens design time and improves reproducibility, but that human oversight remains indispensable. Clinical success depends on manufacturing the right material with validated parameters for the right indication and applying it with an appropriate adhesive or conventional cementation protocol. Accuracy should be defined by its trueness and precision components, marginal fit should be evaluated against clinical acceptability thresholds, and quality control should be maintained at every link of the digital chain. The graded, bioactive, self-healing, and stimuli-responsive materials of the future, together with additively manufactured ceramics, signal a transition from passive to smart materials in restorative dentistry.

candidates.title: Localized Generative Design of Ship Hulls with Diffusion Models and High-Fidelity Assessment
candidates.abstract: Practical ship design requires localized refinement and performance evaluation. This paper presents a reward-directed diffusion framework for localized hull optimization. Parametric masking during dataset generation restricts geometric changes to selected variables, including the bulbous bow and forebody, while preserving full-hull continuity. Surrogate-assisted sequential Monte Carlo sampling targets reduced predicted calm-water resistance, with stability retained through training data and displacement matched during screening. An automated viscous free-surface CFD pipeline, validated against measurements for two benchmark container ships, evaluates a generated variant and GenHull E, a hull refined by a naval architect within the same representation. At matched KRISO Container Ship (KCS) displacement, the generated variant has comparable total resistance at $F_n=0.195$ but 45-50% higher resistance at $F_n=0.250$ and $0.260$, missed by empirical screening. GenHull E achieves 6-8% lower total resistance up to $F_n=0.240$ but higher resistance above $F_n=0.250$ as opposing friction and pressure trends reverse the gains. Aggregating resistance across this crossover can conceal tradeoffs that emerge when friction and pressure components are evaluated separately. The assessment reveals an inability to represent a faired bulbous bow and a reward lacking viscous pressure and stability terms. These findings show how high-fidelity assessment informs improved representations and objectives for physically realizable generative designs.

candidates.title: A novel machining operation strategy prediction method based on self-supervised B-rep learning
candidates.abstract: Manufacturing operation strategy, as a crucial element in part manufacturing, directly impacts processing efficiency and manufacturing quality. Current machine learning-based manufacturing operation decision methods inevitably lose geometric and topological information when converting 3D CAD models into intermediate formats such as point clouds, voxels, or meshes, while also facing the challenge of insufficient training data. To address these issues, this study proposes an innovative hybrid learning approach combining self-supervised pre-training with supervised fine-tuning that learns B-Rep representations from large-scale unlabeled CAD data to achieve manufacturing operation strategy prediction on small-sample datasets. The method consists of two key modules: first, a pre-training model based on an encoder-decoder architecture, where the encoder learns latent representations of CAD model face topological entities, and the decoder reconstructs the signed distance function of model faces; second, a supervised learning phase that utilizes pre-trained facial latent space representations to complete model segmentation tasks based on manufacturing strategies and modeling information using labeled data. Compared to traditional rule-based 3D shape representation sampling methods, directly using B-Rep data representation significantly improves accuracy; compared to existing supervised learning methods based on B-Rep input, the hybrid approach proposed in this study demonstrates superior performance on small-scale training sets.

candidates.title: Look Where You Can: Active View Selection for CAD Reconstruction under Occlusion
candidates.abstract: CAD reconstruction methods assume a luxury reality rarely grants: unrestricted visual access to the object, photographed from any desired angle. Real objects, however, are scene-embedded, bolted against walls, wedged into corners, resting on floors, where the scene renders much of the view sphere unreachable and the remaining views unequally informative. We introduce \textbf{SightCAD}, a framework for parametric CAD reconstruction that treats view feasibility as a first-class constraint. In this work we consider objects from standard CAD benchmarks embedded in realistic indoor scenes with physically derived visibility constraints over a discrete view sphere. A learned view selector must choose $K$ feasible views for a vision--language model (VLM) that generates executable CadQuery code, scored by geometric fidelity of the executed solid. Because reward arrives only after discrete view selection, autoregressive generation, and CAD-kernel execution, we propose a joint training paradigm in which the view selector and the CAD-generation VLM are trained together against this reward. The learned selection policy departs sharply from random, uniform, and coverage-greedy alternatives, outperforming surface-area maximization (SA-max) by up to $6.4$ Intersection-over-Union (IoU) points across budgets $K\in\{1,\dots,5\}$. The full system surpasses strong external baselines on scene-embedded, occluded multi-view renders of DeepCAD and Fusion360 objects ($+21$ and $+17$ effective-mIoU points over the best baseline, respectively), as well as on test-time domain-canonicalized real images from the industrial T-LESS benchmark and on both synthetic and real images from the MP6D industrial metal-parts benchmark, while producing the highest rate of executable programs of any method compared (invalid-code rate ${\leq}1.5\%$).

candidates.title: Healthy Counterfactual Generation via Diffusion Inpainting for Mammography Classification
candidates.abstract: False negatives remain a critical limitation of computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems for breast cancer screening due to delayed detection and treatment. To address this issue, we propose a counterfactual data augmentation strategy that generates healthy mammograms by "erasing" lesions from anomalous images, thereby enriching the training distribution. We train a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model on BI-RADS 1 (healthy) mammograms and use a RePaint-based sampling strategy to inpaint realistic normal tissue within annotated lesion bounding boxes. The resulting healthy counterfactuals replace annotated lesion regions with realistic healthy tissue while preserving patient-specific anatomical structure, as supported by similarity metrics between real and generated images. Image realism was further assessed by radiologists and found to be consistent with the original dataset quality. We evaluate counterfactual augmentation across four representative classifier architectures: a convolutional neural network (ConvNeXt), a vision transformer (ViT), a vision-language model pre-trained on mammogram-report pairs (Mammo-CLIP) and a multi-scale attention-based multiple-instance learning framework (FPN-MIL). Experiments conducted on the VinDr-Mammo dataset show improvements in sensitivity across all architectures, particularly at 80\% fixed specificity, contributing towards more reliable CAD systems for breast cancer. Code is available at: https://github.com/ines03garcia/diffusion-based-counterfactual-generation.

candidates.title: Automated Assembly Instruction Generation from CAD Models Using Grounded Large Language Models: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
candidates.abstract: Assembly documentation is a downstream manufacturing artifact that is still usually authored by interpreting CAD models by hand. Structured product data and large language models are both available, yet studies of CAD interpretation, assembly sequence planning, instruction writing, and human oversight have largely proceeded separately. This paper formulates CAD-grounded assembly instruction generation: the production of natural-language assembly procedures constrained by structured engineering information extracted from CAD models. The proposed framework maps a STEP assembly to a typed ProductGraph intermediate representation, derives a precedence order by deterministic topological sorting, realizes each step as language conditioned only on selected graph context, attaches per-step visual documentation, and applies rule-based and model-assisted checks. PDF export remains disabled until a human reviewer resolves every quality flag. The case study establishes endto-end feasibility on a built-in six-part reference assembly: the pipeline preserves a reported assembly order and carries quantity, material, and torque into an exported manual page. Generalization and geometric validation remain open empirical questions. The contribution is an architecture that separates engineering state, deterministic reasoning, grounded language realization, verification, and human release.

candidates.title: Integrating Sustainability and Life Cycle Assessment into CAD-Driven Product Design: A Systematic Review of Frameworks, Additive Manufacturing Trade-offs and Industry 4.0 Enablers
candidates.abstract: With decarbonisation goals and new ecodesign regulations, life cycle assessment (LCA) is increasingly becoming a function of computer-aided design (CAD). This paper undertakes a systematic review following PRISMA 2020 statement of research related to integrating sustainability and LCA into CAD driven product design. Peer-reviewed journal articles and conference papers published from 2016 to 2026 were retrieved from the databases Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and ScienceDirect (Google Scholar was used as a supporting database) and synthesized in a thematic synthesis. The evidence is presented in six streams: CAD–LCA integration frameworks; sustainable and generative optimisation; design for additive manufacturing (DfAM) and topology optimisation; process-parameter optimisation as a source for life cycle inventory (LCI) data; Industry 4.0 and digital twin (DT) based assessment; and social and organisational enablers of adoption. The review concludes that most of the life cycle impact occurs at the conceptual stage, and that tools for environmental assessment at the conceptual level are not sufficiently mature at the detailed design stage, when geometry and material are fixed. There is a constant dilemma between the material savings possible with topology optimisation and AM, and the extra energy needed to produce structures using these routes does not necessarily mean they have a smaller footprint. Experimental process-optimisation studies demonstrate that the choice of process parameters has a significant effect on the energy used, scrap produced and the consumption of tools, in the cases of machining, moulding, finishing and material-extrusion printing, but the results from these studies are generally not transferred to inventories to use in design tools. The social aspect and the conditions of organisation and skills for adoption, especially in developing economies are under-represented. There are six research priorities identified: uncertainty-aware early-stage LCA, joint material–energy optimisation in DfAM, process-parameter-linked inventory models, interoperability of CAD, LCA, product lifecycle management, and digital twin platforms, AI purpose-built for ecodesign, integration of social and circularity indicators. candidates.title: Retinal and coronary imaging in type 1 diabetes: links between retinopathy and subclinical cardiovascular disease
candidates.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of premature morbidity and mortality in individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), despite advances in glycemic management and cardiovascular prevention. Conventional cardiovascular risk assessment may underestimate risk in T1DM, particularly among younger asymptomatic individuals, highlighting the need for markers of early vascular injury. Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a microvascular complication of T1DM, is increasingly recognized as a marker of systemic vascular dysfunction rather than an isolated ocular disorder. Non-invasive retinal visualization may provide insight into vascular and atherosclerotic disease. This mini-review summarizes evidence linking DR with subclinical coronary artery disease (CAD) and cardiovascular outcomes in T1DM, focusing on coronary artery calcium (CAC) and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Observational and longitudinal studies consistently link DR severity with CAC burden, coronary plaque burden, silent CAD, and cardiovascular outcomes, independent of traditional risk factors. Albuminuria and diabetic kidney disease may provide complementary evidence of a broader microvascular phenotype associated with cardiovascular risk. Advances in retinal imaging, including optical coherence tomography angiography and artificial intelligence-based oculomics, support the role of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular risk prediction. CAC scoring remains valuable for detecting subclinical coronary atherosclerosis, while CCTA characterizes calcified and non-calcified plaque. Emerging evidence suggests that integrating retinal and microvascular markers with coronary imaging may improve identification of asymptomatic individuals at increased cardiovascular risk and support intervention. Although data are observational and prospective validation is required, multimodal strategies combining clinical risk factors, retinal biomarkers, albuminuria, CAC, and CCTA may enhance cardiovascular risk stratification in T1DM.

candidates.title: End-to-End Autonomous Generation of Human Assembly Plans
candidates.abstract: Turning a CAD design into an assembly plan is still largely done by hand, requiring engineers to reason about geometric feasibility, tool access, stability, and the ergonomics of human assembly. In this work, we encode long-established design for assembly (DfA) principles into a contained, end-to-end approach for generating assembly plans. Our approach takes only a mesh assembly and produces either a step-by-step assembly manual or a structured failure report, requiring no joint metadata, fastener annotations, or additional information. Four major components of a manufacturing plan are addressed autonomously: an assembly tool list, the assembly sequence and subassemblies, an assembly manual, and design feedback for improving assemblability. For determining the sequence plan, we systematically disassemble the object in a physics simulator and apply a cost function that encodes DfA principles. Manual generation, tool labelling, and assembly feedback rely primarily on multimodal large language models. Compared with a baseline that always removes the outermost part first from Tian et al., DfA-aware sequence planning reduces simulated assembly time, measured with a robot-arm assembly-time proxy, by 35% on 136 assemblies of 5 to 30 parts. The correct tool is selected for 88.6% of assembly steps. A vision-language model judge compares the generated manuals against ablated variants, identifying which page elements carry the information a reader needs. The presented approach and open-source code are available for use by engineers or AI agents looking to rapidly accelerate the creation of manufacturing plans for a given product design.

candidates.title: Confidence-based classification of clinically significant prostate cancer on biparametric MRI using Monte Carlo dropout and Grad-CAM visualization
candidates.abstract: Objective Accurate early diagnosis of Clinically Significant prostate cancer (csPCa) is crucial for improving patient survival rates. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable, confidence-based deep learning model for csPCa classification using biparametric MRI (bpMRI). Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on bpMRI data from 410 patients. A classification model was constructed using the visual geometry group 16-layer (VGG-16) network, incorporating gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) for visual interpretability, Monte Carlo Dropout (MC-Dropout) for uncertainty estimation, and a rejection mechanism. The model’s performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the ROC curve (AUC). Results Across all predictions, the confidence-based model achieved an overall accuracy of 79.3% before rejection. At a confidence threshold of 0.8, 80.8% of predictions were retained, among which the selective accuracy was 94.6%, with 99 false-positive and 2 false-negative predictions. Besides, the model’s accuracy outperformed that of a senior radiologist (94.6% vs 90.8%). Qualitative Grad-CAM visualization demonstrated that the classifier frequently assigned high activation to MRI regions considered suspicious for csPCa; however, quantitative spatial agreement with lesion annotations was not assessed. Conclusion This confidence-based model identifies csPCa lesions and provides reliable confidence scores without pixel-level annotations. By rejecting uncertain predictions, it enhances the transparency and safety of clinical decision-making.

candidates.title: CADFather: Autonomous CAD Reconstruction through Coordinated Tool Use
candidates.abstract: Reconstructing an editable CAD model from a 3D shape remains a challenging engineering task. Existing methods can propose CAD operations, but no single source of proposals works equally well across different part geometries and stages of reconstruction. We introduce CADFather, an autonomous agentic system that coordinates complementary tools to recover parametric CAD programs from 3D meshes. A vision-language assistant inspects renders of the target and intermediate reconstructions, then decides which candidate CAD programs to extend, which tools to invoke, how many proposals to generate, and when to finish. Learned and algorithmic tools propose CAD operations, while numerical optimization refines the parameters of existing programs. Proposed or refined programs are executed and evaluated to provide feedback for subsequent decisions. The agent maintains alternative candidate programs for each target part and preserves the best valid result throughout reconstruction. CADFather uses pretrained generation and assistant models without additional training. We evaluate reconstruction quality and execution validity on the full DeepCAD, Fusion360, and MCB test sets, as well as on CADENA-Bench, CADBench, and BenchCAD. We additionally analyze computational cost and the trade-off between cost and reconstruction quality.

candidates.title: PrimitiveCAD: An LLM-Based Point-to-CAD Reconstruction with Primitive-Aware Tokenization and Operation Alignment
candidates.abstract: Large-model-based point-to-CAD generation holds immense potential for advancing industrial design and enhancing 3D modeling efficiency. However, most existing methods approach the problem as a general point-cloud encoding and token prediction task, neglecting the tokenization and supervision specifically for CAD-related primitives. As a result, these methods often struggle to accurately reconstruct the intricate primitive structures. To address this limitation, we propose PrimitiveCAD, a novel multi-stage paradigm for point-to-CAD reconstruction that enhances the geometric accuracy of generated CAD models while better preserving critical geometric features. First, we introduce a primitive-aware point cloud tokenization model, enabling the system to learn more robust geometric representations from CAD point clouds. Next, we perform supervised finetuning on a large language model (LLM) and introduce an operation alignment loss to align key CAD operation frequencies, thereby improving the preservation of global shape features. Finally, we incorporate reinforcement learning (RL) and introduce a feature-line alignment reward to further reduce stochasticity and enhance the fine-grained preservation of geometric features. Experiments on the DeepCAD and Fusion360 datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in code validity, geometric accuracy, and geometric feature preservation.

candidates.title: Learning to Simulate Individuals from Macro Social Signals
candidates.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate how individuals respond to new situations, yet the behavioral reasoning behind these responses is either inherited from pretraining or learned from individual-level annotations, which offer limited behavioral diversity and little supervision of the reasoning itself. We propose to learn behavioral reasoning from prediction markets, whose price trajectories record how populations respond to real-world events at scale. We introduce macro2mind, which trains a language model with GRPO using market signals. A social behavioral decomposition makes behavioral reasoning an explicit step of forecasting: the model infers representative groups of market participants, predicts how each interprets the news and updates its beliefs, reasons about their interactions, and aggregates these responses into a price. A hindsight-regret curriculum with difficulty-aware sampling focuses training on transitions where hindsight-identified groups substantially improve the forecast while prioritizing examples that remain learnable for the current policy. The learned reasoning applies to user simulation without further training. On SWM-Bench, macro2mind achieves state-of-the-art directional accuracy and correlation on Polymarket. Trained on market data, it transfers zero-shot to four user-simulation benchmarks (Humanual, OvertonBench, PRISM, and CAD) and has competitive performance among zero-shot methods. Used as a data generator, macro2mind also raises a downstream simulator's accuracy on unseen users by 15.5 points, outperforming data generated by its backbone by 13.2 points.

candidates.title: A face-level machining operation strategy prediction method for prismatic parts based on transformer and B-Rep learning
candidates.abstract: Driven by increasing product customisation and shortened product life cycles, modern manufacturing places higher demands on the efficiency and consistency of machining operation strategy selection. Traditional strategy selection relies heavily on expert knowledge and manual intervention, resulting in limited efficiency and the risk of human error. B-Rep-based learning methods can better preserve the geometric and topological information of CAD models, but existing graph neural network-based approaches mainly rely on layer-wise message passing within local neighbourhoods and remain limited in modelling dependencies between topologically distant regions. To address this issue, this paper proposes BRepMSNet, which integrates the B-Rep data structure with the Transformer architecture for direct face-level machining operation strategy prediction from 3D CAD models. BRepMSNet takes directed coedges as local topology centres, gathers face, edge, and coedge information through predefined topological walks, and organises local B-Rep neighbourhoods into coedge-centred topology tokens. Multi-head kernelized linear self-attention is then employed to establish global contextual relationships among different local topological neighbourhoods, jointly modelling local topological structures and long-range contextual information. Experimental results show that BRepMSNet achieves an accuracy of 98.02% on the machining operation strategy prediction task and also demonstrates competitive performance on multiple public datasets.

candidates.title: INTELLIGENT CAD/CAM INTEGRATION FOR ADAPTIVE MANUFACTURING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF AI AND IOT FRAMEWORKS IN INDUSTRY 4.0
candidates.abstract: The union of Artificial Intelligence and the Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming the way Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) systems are used in the Industry 4.0 production process. Based on the PRISMA 2020 reporting framework (Page et al., 2021), this report is a systematic literature review on the intelligent integration of CAD and CAM technologies in adaptive manufacturing. Based on a structured search of major scientific databases, a curated list of peer-reviewed studies was analysed thematically to address five research questions related to designing with AI, toolpath optimisation using AI, IoT/IIoT architectures for real-time adaptive control, interoperability standards and barriers to AI adoption in specific sectors. AI models, especially deep learning, graph neural networks and reinforcement learning, have led the way in recent research and development on automatic feature recognition and toolpath generation, while digital twins, edge computing and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) sensor networks are more and more being used to implement predictive maintenance and closed-loop adaptive control in the shop floor. The design phase is also starting to change with Generative AI to enable manufacturability constraints to be built in earlier in the CAD process. The literature, however, shows that there are still significant gaps that need to be addressed: AI models deployed outside of the simulation environment are not adaptable in real-time, training datasets are not standardized and openly shared, and there are interoperability protocols that are still quite disjointed, and resources for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) looking to use these technologies are still limited. To situate these gaps in a particular developing-economy context, this review is also supplemented by a series of recently published empirical studies. The review suggests that interoperability standards, Human Safety for Industry 5.0 design principles, cybersecurity, and sustainable practice are the key factors that need to be coordinated for the intelligent CAD/CAM-IoT integration to be fully realised, and it presents a roadmap of future research directions for adaptive and connected manufacturing ecosystems.

candidates.title: CADForge: Agentic Single-View CAD Reconstruction with Explicit Geometry Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Reconstructing editable parametric CAD models from a single-view image is of great practical value for modern manufacturing, yet remains challenging due to incomplete geometric observations and complex inter-part relationships. To address it, we propose CADForge, an agentic framework that progressively converts a single image into CadQuery programs. CADForge decomposes an object into CAD-meaningful components and performs explicit geometric reasoning for each component, a process that first identifies CAD-relevant constraints and then translates them into precise modeling parameters through mathematical code. The inferred parameters then drive component-wise synthesis of executable CadQuery programs, with a review agent evaluating the resulting geometry and providing targeted feedback for iterative refinement. To further improve robustness and efficiency, CADForge incorporates a failure-guided toolkit construction mechanism to distill accumulated experience into tools, and maintains a compact parametric CAD memory for retrieving modeling context on demand. Experiments on diverse single- and multi-part objects show that CADForge consistently outperforms existing baselines in reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality, demonstrating an effective approach to accurate single-view CAD reconstruction.

candidates.title: LMBuild: Evaluating LLM Agents for Generating Buildable and Functional Structures
candidates.abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly capable of generating complex 3D structures, with the potential to reshape how objects are designed and realized in the physical world. Yet, producing elegant geometry is fundamentally different from producing objects that can be built and perform their intended functions. Existing evaluations largely focus on geometric quality while overlooking physical realizability. We introduce LMBuild, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on generating buildable and functional structures. LMBuild represents generated objects as assembled structures comprising part decompositions, joints, materials, and sequences. To support reproducible evaluation, we provide a unified framework consisting of: (1) an interactive environment in which agents can use tools to retrieve, create, and place components to construct objects; (2) a curated benchmark that repurposes established CAD datasets and augments them with knowledge from Wikipedia; and (3) a evaluation framework covering structural soundness, functional affordance, design quality, and physical realization. Evaluations across 30 systems reveal several intriguing findings: (a) Soundness and alignment are no longer the primary bottlenecks for frontier closed-source models, while functional affordance and physical operability remain substantially more challenging; (b) stronger models more effectively create new components, whereas weaker models tend to rely on retrieval; and (c) providing functional specifications substantially improves part completeness, kinematics, and physical operability. These results show that generating real-world structures requires deeper reasoning about functional affordances, mechanics, and designing and creating novel components. We expect LMBuild to provide a foundation for measuring progress and incentivizing research toward agents that generate buildable and functional structures.

candidates.title: Dependable AI-Assisted Engineering: A Formal Framework for AI Participation and Assurance in Safety-Critical Workflows
candidates.abstract: Generative AI can produce engineering artefacts, but generation alone does not determine whether or how those artefacts should enter safety-critical workflows. This paper develops a formal framework for assigning AI participation and assurance at the level of individual workflow units. Each unit has a participation and assurance record covering its engineering requirement, an approved operational formalization where applicable, the applicable mechanism, fallback where applicable, evidence obligations and the applicable guarantee, plus a deployment-readiness status. The framework distinguishes deterministic verification, statistically calibrated admission, authorized human judgement supported by AI advice, authorized human adjudication of AI-produced artefacts, retained deterministic tool paths and explicit non-participation; these arrangements carry different kinds of guarantee rather than levels on a common scale. The framework also separates formalization fidelity from verifier soundness, provides a staged classification and readiness procedure, and derives conditions for comparing a gated AI-assisted unit with an incumbent process under recurring-population assumptions. We instantiate and apply the framework in an executed 17-unit wing-spar structural-analysis workflow combining deterministically gated AI-generated CAD, retained deterministic computation and human judgement. The AI-generated CAD program passed all 23 deterministic checks and was admitted at the first attempt. Favourable stress magnitudes did not suffice to pass the stress criteria where the predeclared mesh-convergence evidence was insufficient; those criteria were instead referred to engineering judgement. The case demonstrates selective AI participation and explicit evidence handling at unit level; no claim is made of workflow-level dependability, certification, structural safety or productivity.

candidates.title: CUAWright: A Minimal Unified Interface for Digital Agents
candidates.abstract: The prevailing approach to computer-use agents couples a model with a domain-specific harness: a browser or desktop environment equipped with human engineered tools that are fixed before task execution. As models' coding capabilities improve, the GUI native and static harness prevents them from direct programmatic operation on system state, as well as flexible construction of tools. To this end, we introduce CUAWright, a minimal terminal harness of roughly 3K lines of code that uses bash commands as its sole action interface, and a file system as its evolvable space for dynamically creating tools and managing the context. We conduct comprehensive experiments across a wide range of digital tasks, and demonstrate that by giving the agent a minimal, programmable interface, it achieves substantially stronger results compared to their GUI or hybrid CLI interface across a wide range of tasks. On OSWorld 2.0, CUAWright delivers a 33.2% relative improvement in partial reward while reducing estimated cost by 37.5% compared with the published GPT-5.5 baseline. On Online-Mind2Web and the long horizon Odysseys benchmark, CUAWright substantially outperforms GUI native harness by 4.7% and 44.0% in success rate, respectively. Furthermore, we found the gains extend to CAD applications that require accurate visual understanding and CLI interaction: on CADGenBench and BenchCAD, our unified harness yields 8.1%-41.6% relative improvements over other CLI based harnesses with GPT-5.5. Together, these results suggest digital environments are far more programmable than their GUI interfaces imply, and a minimal terminal-focused harness is the key for better performance and efficiency.

candidates.title: Hybrid CNN–Graph Transformer Encoder with Autoregressive Decoding for CAPP-GPT
candidates.abstract: Automating Computer-Aided Process Planning (CAPP) remains a significant challenge in digital manufacturing, particularly the direct generation of optimal Manufacturing sequences from Boundary Representation (B-Rep) CAD models or Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) trees. Existing deep learning methods often fall short, either by sacrificing geometric and topological fidelity through conversion to intermediate representations or by focusing primarily on feature classification rather than full sequential plan generation. This paper presents a proof-of concept encoder–decoder Transformer architecture designed to address this gap. The encoder extracts local geometric information using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) applied to UV-grid samplings of CAD faces, enriched with explicit attributes of each face and edge (e.g., type and adjacency). In parallel, global relational context is captured by representing the CAD structure as a graph and processing it with a Graph Transformer. Through this joint representation, the encoder recognizes Manufacturing features, which are then passed to the Transformer-based decoder that autoregressively generates complete and optimal manufacturing plans token by token. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a challenging case study with interacting geometric features, where our model successfully produces logically consistent and optimal Manufacturing sequences; the focus of the case study, though, is on the decoder part of the architecture. The overall framework still provides a promising direction for CAPP directly from native CAD data.

candidates.title: StepCAD: Mesh-to-CAD Code Generation via LLM Policy and Geometry-Guided Search
candidates.abstract: Recovering executable CAD programs from 3D meshes is challenging due to the compositional nature of CAD construction and the interaction between discrete modeling choices and continuous parameters. Many learning-based methods predict complete programs in a single pass and rely predominantly on sketch-extrude representations, limiting operation diversity and opportunities to correct geometric errors during reconstruction. We introduce StepCAD, a generative optimization approach that combines a state-conditioned CAD policy with geometry-guided search. Given an input mesh, the policy predicts construction actions conditioned on both target and intermediate geometry, and an IoU-guided tree search refines the resulting program through local edits. We also introduce ARCADE-1.5M, a large-scale dataset of 1.5M executable CAD programs spanning diverse operations, sequences with a maximum length of 150+ counted operations, and 12.5M intermediate state-action transitions. Experiments across multiple CAD reconstruction benchmarks show that StepCAD achieves state-of-the-art geometric reconstruction accuracy with consistently high validity, yielding up to 87.2% relative IoU improvement over the strongest evaluated baseline, with particularly large gains on complex shapes. candidates.title: Diffusion transformers with hybrid conditioning for structural optimization
candidates.abstract: Abstract This work presents a diffusion transformer framework for data-driven structural topology optimization that combines the accuracy of physics-based methods with the efficiency of generative deep learning. Conventional density-based approaches which use the solid isotropic material with penalization (SIMP) scheme with a gradient update require repeated finite element analyses at every iteration, making large-scale or real-time optimization computationally expensive. We propose a hybrid conditioning diffusion transformer (DiT) model that learns to generate near-optimal topologies directly from problem definitions, eliminating iterative analysis during inference. The model integrates spatially distributed conditioning through concatenated stress and strain fields and global conditioning via adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN) using scalar descriptors such as load position, magnitude, and prescribed volume fraction. A dataset of 30,000 two-dimensional SIMP-optimized structures was generated for training and evaluation. Results demonstrate that the proposed DiT achieves less than 1% compliance errors relative to ground-truth SIMP solutions while maintaining accurate volume fractions and structural connectivity. Deterministic DDIM sampling enables high-fidelity topology generation in seconds using as few as five denoising steps, enabling near-real-time performance. The hybrid conditioning diffusion transformer thus provides an efficient and scalable alternative to traditional topology optimization methods, with strong potential for integration into interactive computer-aided design workflows.

candidates.title: Performance of large language models in complex coronary artery disease decision-making and potential improvement strategy in a real-world cohort
candidates.abstract: Objective Previous studies have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can achieve performance comparable to multidisciplinary heart teams (HTs) in coronary revascularisation decision-making but limited by population bias. We aimed to assess LLMs’ performance in complex coronary artery disease (CAD) decision-making using a real-world cohort and to explore the potential improvement strategy.Methods Patients with stable CAD and angiographically confirmed three-vessel or left main disease randomly selected from a consecutive angiography registry study were included in this cross-sectional study. ChatGPT-4.1 was used to provide five-category treatment decisions based on inputted patient information and a prompt most commonly used by real-world patients. The primary outcome was the agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations. Three predefined prompting strategies were further evaluated for their potential to enhance agreement rates.Results A total of 564 patients were included. The agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations was 47.0% based on initial prompt. LLM performed poorly in further testing (sensitivity=0.0%) decision. LLM performed well in patients with Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery score ≥33 (94.1%) but poorly in 23–32 (61.7%) and 0–22 (20.9%). After using prompting strategies, the agreement rate increased significantly (79.3%, p<0.001).Discussion Simple patient-style queries cannot independently generate reliable decisions for real-world complex revascularisation scenarios. While prompt engineering and subgroup analysis can partially improve LLM’s performance, the potential safety risk remains emphasised.Conclusion Among a real-world cohort of patients with complex CAD, the agreement rate of decision-making between LLM and HTs was only half, but could be improved with appropriate prompts.

candidates.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence-Driven Augmentation With Deep Feature Fusion Model for Rare Disease Detection and Classification
candidates.abstract: Rare disease detection focuses on identifying rare health conditions that affect a tiny fraction of people. Detection is challenging because symptoms are often ambiguous and information is limited. In recent years, retinal diseases have become a serious problem worldwide. Progressing a computer-assisted diagnosis (CAD) method is highly beneficial and functional for ophthalmologists. Proper detection and treatment can save eye vision. Deep learning (DL) has advanced across various scientific fields and is leveraged for numerous healthcare tasks. This research presents a Generative Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Adaptive Feature Fusion Network for Rare Retinal Disease Detection (GAIAFF-RRDD) technique assists ophthalmologists by allowing early and precise detection of rare retinal diseases, thus enhancing clinical decision-making and decreasing diagnostic workload. The GAIAFF-RRDD technique integrates advanced pre-processing, augmentation, feature fusion, and classification strategies to improve diagnostic accuracy in retinal image analysis. A conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) is employed to augment realistic images and overcome the limited availability of images for rare retinal diseases. Furthermore, adaptive feature fusion is performed by combining features extracted from CapsNet, DenseNet-121, and VGG-16 methods. Finally, a variational autoencoder (VAE)-based classification technique is used to classify rare retinal diseases accurately. To ensure improved performance of the GAIAFF-RRDD methodology, an extensive simulation analysis is conducted using the RFMiD dataset. The comparison study of the GAIAFF-RRDD methodology showed an accuracy of 93.92% compared with existing approaches. Therefore, the proposed model is found to be a robust tool for automated and accurate rare disease detection process.

candidates.title: Comparison of Integrated Versus Sequential Artificial Intelligence–Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis Systems in Breast Ultrasound: A Prospective Pilot Study on Examination Time, Reproducibility, and Diagnostic Performance
candidates.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To compare integrated and sequential artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis (AI-CAD) systems in terms of examination time, reproducibility, and diagnostic performance in breast ultrasound (US). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective single-center study included women who underwent breast US at a breast imaging center between February and March 2025. Two real-time AI-CAD systems were evaluated: an integrated system providing simultaneous lesion detection and diagnosis during scanning, and a sequential system in which lesion detection and diagnostic assessment were performed separately. Examination time was assessed in patients who underwent paired breast US examinations with both AI-CAD systems during the same visit, with randomized examination order. Reproducibility was assessed by applying both systems twice to the same breast lesions. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: Examination time analysis included 97 patients and showed longer examination time with sequential AI-CAD than with integrated AI-CAD (P < .001), regardless of examination order. Reproducibility analysis included 145 patients with 215 lesions and showed almost perfect agreement between the first and second acquisitions for both systems (integrated vs. sequential: κ = 0.81 vs. 0.83). For the comparison between the first and second acquisitions, κ values for the integrated versus sequential systems were 0.92 versus 0.76 for malignant lesions, 0.79 versus 0.84 for mass lesions, and 1.00 versus 0.75 for nonmass lesions. However, agreement patterns varied across other scan-plane comparisons. Diagnostic performance analysis included 242 patients. Integrated AI-CAD showed higher sensitivity (integrated vs. sequential: 87.6% vs. 76.9%; P < .001), whereas sequential AI-CAD showed higher specificity (integrated vs. sequential: 74.2% vs. 90.0%; P < .001). AUC did not differ between the two systems. CONCLUSION: Integrated and sequential AI-CAD systems showed complementary strengths in breast US. Integrated AI-CAD favored shorter examination time and higher sensitivity, whereas sequential AI-CAD favored higher specificity, with reproducibility differing according to lesion type.

candidates.title: Revolutionizing Failure Analysis: Physics-Guided AI for Advanced Technology CAD Alignment
candidates.abstract: Abstract This paper presents an automated system for accurately aligning infrared (IR) and computer-aided design (CAD) images. Accurate alignment is an important prerequisite for successful defect localization in failure analysis (FA). Building on the authors' prior study at a different semiconductor technology node, the approach leverages in-depth knowledge of the semiconductor fabrication process, deep neural networks, and computer vision algorithms to achieve precise alignment. The results demonstrate high alignment accuracy using synthetic IR images.

candidates.title: Deep Neural Network-Driven Reliability Assessment Methodology for Total Ionizing Dose Effects in FDSOI MOSFETs
candidates.abstract: This work investigates the effects of total ionizing dose (TID) on 22 nm FDSOI MOSFET devices through combined technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations and actual TID irradiation experiments, establishing a comprehensive dataset of radiation-induced degradation characteristics. By utilizing both simulated and experimental radiation data as training foundations, this research developed and optimized a deep neural network (DNN) capable of conducting efficient and accurate reliability analysis of TID effects under various radiation conditions, with demonstrated effectiveness in predicting device performance degradation across different TID ranges. The methodology integrates physical simulations with deep learning approaches, where TCAD simulations and irradiation experiments capture fundamental device physics under radiation exposure, while the DNN enables rapid performance prediction. The resulting framework achieves superior prediction accuracy while significantly reducing computational costs compared to conventional simulation methods, providing a powerful solution for evaluating electronic device reliability in complex radiation environments.

candidates.title: OP-CAD: On-Policy Clean-Audio Distillation for Robust Audio-Visual Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Omni-modal large language models deployed in real-world environments encounter external noise that can interfere with their perception and understanding of multimodal inputs. We study their robustness in audio-visual understanding, focusing on question answering under environmental noise and competing speech. The challenge is to resist acoustic interference while preserving useful audio evidence. On-policy distillation provides dense teacher feedback on student-generated responses, but uniform token weighting does not explicitly prioritize positions affected by acoustic interference. We introduce OP-CAD (On-Policy Clean-Audio Distillation), a curriculum-based privileged self-distillation framework for robust audio-visual understanding. Training progresses from mild to severe environmental noise and competing speech, with selective token-level supervision at each stage. The student generates responses from corrupted audio-visual input, while a frozen teacher uses clean audio and the verified answer to supervise the same response prefixes. To allocate this supervision, OP-CAD compares teacher predictions under clean, corrupted, and visual-only contexts without revealing the answer. These matched comparisons measure sensitivity to audio removal and corruption; a bounded weighting rule emphasizes positions identified by either signal while retaining supervision throughout the response. OP-CAD outperforms the compared methods across all evaluated noise conditions. Paired analyses further show improved preservation of clean-correct answers under strong interference, with no observed aggregate clean-accuracy penalty. These results demonstrate the value of directing clean-teacher supervision toward acoustically sensitive predictions for robust audio-visual reasoning.

candidates.title: Comparison of AI-generated and conventional CAD/CAM crown designs: An in vitro evaluation
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can automate crown design, but its accuracy and function require comparison with conventional CAD/CAM. Therefore, it is of interest to compare the both workflows on 30 standardized mandibular first-molar preparations. AI shortened design time (1.73 ą 0.43 vs 5.63 ą 1.14 min; p<0.001) and reduced whole-crown RMS deviation. AI reduced marginal gap (60.3 ą 14.2 versus 68.8 ą 13.0 ľm; p<0.001), while conventional CAD was better proximally. Thus, functional contacts were comparable, supporting AI as an efficient design aid with final technician or clinician verification.

candidates.title: A Study on Innovation Strategies in Contemporary Jewelry Design Using Generative Artificial Intelligence
candidates.abstract: 본 연구의 목적은 생성형 인공지능(AI) 기술을 활용한 현대 주얼리 디자인의 혁신 전략을 고찰하고, AI 기술이 디자인 창작과 제작 과정에 미치는 영향과 활용 가능성을 분석하는 데 있다. 최근 생성형 AI의 발전은 디자인 분야 전반에 새로운 창작 환경을 제시하고 있으며, 현대 주얼리 디자인에서도 아이디어 발상, 형태 생성, 맞춤형 제작, 디지털 제작 공정 등 다양한 영역으로 활용 범위가 확대되고 있다. 이에 본 연구는 생성형 AI 기술이 현대 주얼리 디자인에 가져온 변화와 혁신 전략을 체계적으로 분석하고 그 의의를 도출하고자 하였다. 연구방법은 문헌연구와 내용분석을 중심으로 진행하였다. 국내외 학술논문, 전문서적, 학회자료 및 산업보고서를 검토하여 생성형 AI의 개념과 특성을 정리하고, 현대 주얼리 디자인과의 연계 가능성을 고찰하였다. 또한 생성형 AI 도구와 보조 디자인 시스템의 기능 및 활용 특성을 분석하여 기술 활용의 특징을 도출하고, 이를 바탕으로 현대 주얼리 디자인의 혁신 전략을 종합적으로 분석하였다. 연구 결과, 생성형 AI는 현대 주얼리 디자인의 기획, 설계 및 제작 전 과정에서 활용되며 디자인 프로세스를 확장하는 핵심 기술로 확인되었다. 내용분석에서는 생성형 AI가 다양한 디자인 아이디어를 신속하게 제안하고, 복합적인 형태 생성과 사용자 맞춤형 디자인을 구현하며, CAD와 3D 프린팅 등 디지털 제작 기술과 연계되어 제작 효율성과 표현 가능성을 향상시키는 것으로 나타났다. 이를 바탕으로 현대 주얼리 디자인의 혁신 전략은 첫째, 사용자의 취향과 요구를 반영하는 개별 맞춤형 제작과 둘째, 생성형 AI, CAD, 파라메트릭 모델링 및 3D 프린팅 기술을 활용한 기술 중심의 형태 및 공정 혁신으로 구분할 수 있었다. 개별 맞춤형 제작은 소비자 중심의 디자인 환경을 확대하고 감성적 가치를 높이는 데 기여하였으며, 형태 및 공정 혁신은 복합적인 형태 구현, 설계 오류 감소, 제작 기간 단축 및 생산 효율 향상에 기여하는 것으로 분석되었다. 결론적으로 생성형 AI는 현대 주얼리 디자인에서 창의성 확장, 맞춤형 디자인 구현 및 제작 공정의 효율화를 실현하는 핵심 기술로서 디자인 혁신을 촉진하는 중요한 역할을 수행하고 있다. 특히 AI는 디자이너를 대체하는 기술이 아니라 창의적 사고를 지원하고 디지털 제작 환경과 연계하는 협업 도구로서의 가능성을 보여준다. 본 연구는 생성형 AI 기반 현대 주얼리 디자인의 혁신 전략을 체계적으로 정리하였다는 점에서 학술적 의의를 가지며, 향후 AI 기술과 주얼리 디자인의 융합에 관한 후속 연구를 위한 기초자료로 활용될 수 있을 것으로 기대한다.

candidates.title: CANTO: CAD-Native Transformer Operators for AI-Aided Engineering
candidates.abstract: Modern engineering systems, from automobiles to aircraft, are designed by using precise, continuous parametric computer-aided design (CAD) models. Evaluating design changes through numerical simulation requires meshing the continuous geometry, a computationally expensive and often brittle process that can require manual intervention and replaces the continuous representation with a discrete approximation. Most neural surrogates accelerate the simulation, but inherit this representation gap by relying on meshes, point clouds, voxels, or other sampled approximations of geometry. We introduce CANTO, a transformer neural operator that maps directly from continuous CAD geometry to physical fields, without meshing the input geometry. We develop a theoretical framework for learning operators from geometric manifolds to function spaces of physical fields, representing geometry through sequences of parametric patches. CANTO instantiates this framework by directly tokenizing non-uniform rational B-spline (NURBS) patches from their control points, knot vectors, and weights, and predicts continuous surface and volume fields at arbitrary query locations. We evaluate CANTO on four automotive and aircraft aerodynamics industry benchmarks: AhmedML, WindsorML, DrivAerML, and HiLiftAeroML. CANTO achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on most evaluated surface and volume prediction tasks, including a 19.8% reduction in surface-pressure relative $L_2$ error compared with AB-UPT on HiLiftAeroML. Differentiability with respect to CAD parameters further enables gradient-based inverse design of designs. On AhmedML, CANTO identifies designs with 4.4 to 20.4% lower drag than the best dataset designs satisfying the same volume and lift constraints, with the improvements verified using the same CFD setup used to generate the original dataset.

candidates.title: Perception and Adoption of AI-Generated Designs Among Registered Architects in Lagos, Nigeria
candidates.abstract: The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming architectural design processes, yet empirical evidence on Architects’ perception and adoption of AI-generated designs in developing-country contexts remains limited. This study investigates registered Architects’ perceptions of AI-generated designs and examines the factors influencing the adoption and application of AI tools in architectural practice in Lagos, Nigeria. A mixed-method research design was employed, combining a cross-sectional questionnaire survey with semi-structured interviews. Data were obtained from 117 of the 277 registered Architects practising in Lagos State and analysed using descriptive statistics, content analysis and thematic analysis, with triangulation used to integrate quantitative and qualitative findings. The findings reveal high awareness and understanding of AI technologies (M=3.19, SD=1.28), but relatively limited practical competence and experience. Architects predominantly perceive AI-generated designs as conceptual and creative aids (M=3.23, SD=1.24), rather than finished professional outputs. Consequently, AI adoption is concentrated in early design activities, particularly rapid client visualisation and the generation of design alternatives (M=3.15 each). Integration into detailed design and documentation remains constrained by interoperability challenges with CAD and BIM platforms (M=2.97, SD=1.08). Ethical concerns surrounding authorship, accountability, professional responsibility and contextual relevance further moderate adoption, while perceived usefulness, workflow efficiency, innovation and creative support encourage it. Conversely, concerns about reliability, practice is shaped by interacting technological, professional and contextual factors. It highlights the need for targeted professional training, appropriate regulatory frameworks and context-sensitive strategies for responsible AI integration into architectural education and practice.
